<feedback>
This is the same code I reviewed last round, and my verdict stands: it is correct against the spec and ready to ship. I looked again for anything I missed and found no new correctness problem. I could not compile or run it in this read-only turn, so this rests on reading the code alone.

- **Type narrowing:** `values.values().next()` returns an `IteratorResult<string, …>`. After the `!match.done` check, TypeScript narrows `match.value` to `string`, so the returned value is typed correctly.
- **Trimming:** `request.trim()` removes all ECMAScript whitespace, including NBSP and BOM. That fits "trim whitespace" and matches the spec's choice of JavaScript built-ins.
- **Two edge cases, both handled:**
  - A select option whose category is the literal string `"model"` but whose id is something like `x` is picked by the exact-category path before any tokenizing. That is the intended order.
  - An option with category `"mode"` is never used as a fallback for `"model"`, because the fallback rejects every nonempty category.
- **One remaining assumption, which I would accept:** `"options" in item` treats any object with an `options` key as a group. The spec says all inputs conform to the types, so this is safe.
</feedback>
